text.p: SYDNEY, July 14 - Gold and oil prices were slightly stronger on Friday and wheat prices were mixed among commodities of Australian interest, while supply tightness was the focus in other metals. The CRB index was up 0.82 at 233.52.
METALS - During an otherwise fairly routine day in commodity markets the London Metal Exchange (LME) admitted on Friday it was keeping an eye on trading activity in its copper and zinc contracts.
While pointing out that the LME monitors all its contracts Chief-Executive David King told Reuters: "We are taking an interest in copper and zinc, which are sensitive at the moment."
The copper market is currently finely balanced and zinc stocks have fallen considerably, he said.

Traders said that copper activity recently has become more and more focused on a developing supply tightness for delivery dates around the middle of July and this was probably the reason for closer monitoring by the Exchange.

With investors, not wanting to be caught short of metal during that period, coming in to buy or borrow material the price of nearby delivery was trading around $140 above the level of benchmark three months delivery, which was at $2,284 a tonne.
In zinc a similar situation was developing but for delivery dates a couple of months ahead, in September.

Traders reasoned that if stocks continued to fall metal may be difficult to get hold of by the end of the summer. Premiums for September delivery were running around $12 above the three months delivery which was around $1,485 a tonne.

Among other metals, aluminium paid little lasting attention to a 6,900-tonne stock increase, whch was believed to reflect off-warrant consignment metal being registered. Last trade was at $1,582, up $12.
Nickel prices came to life during the afternoon rings and kerb, ending $115 firmer at $6,965.
Lead progressed higher as well, albeit slowly, helped by its sister metal zinc, and by the end of the kerb was standing $7 higher at $667. The market's target is still $675.
Tin business was largely subdued, before a late mark-up on the kerb. Three months concluded at $5,550, up $30.
Alloy was neglected for most of the session, closing at a stable $1,420/30 a tonne.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals ended mostly higher Friday, on fund shortcovering in both gold and platinum group metals (PGMs), but volumes were only moderate. COMEX August gold ended up $1.40 at $322.20 an ounce, after climbing above Thursday's high at $322.20 late in the day, and edging up to a session high at $323.10.
The COMEX August/December spread narrowed further to around $3.20 an ounce, from $3.50 Thursday and $4.40 last Thursday before the Independence Day holiday weekend.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $321.00/60, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $319.50 and the New York close Thursday around $319.60/10.

Gold fixed at a 12 year low early Wednesday this week at $315.75 in London, after news of a further central bank gold sale last week. The Reserve Bank of Australia sold 167 tonnes of gold, two-thirds of its reserves, with deliveries occurring in June, August and September this year.
While further shortcovering may ensue next week, as the gold market works off its technically oversold condition, sentiment remains bearish, analysts said.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed mixed despite perceptions that a USDA forecast for 1997 U.S. winter wheat production was bearish, traders said. Analysts at a CBOT press briefing Friday said the CBOT soft red winter wheat futures contracts may have fallen to their seasonal harvest lows in anticipation of a large U.S. winter wheat crop.
CBOT September wheat dropped early to a session low of $3.23 per bushel, just above the contract low of $3.21 that was set Tuesday.

USDA on Friday in its July wheat production forecast, pegged 1997 U.S. winter wheat production at 1.781 billion bushels, above an average of analysts' estimates for 1.687 billion bushels. But USDA also pegged total wheat production at 2.431 billion bushels, below the average analyst expectation for 2.433 billion. CBOT wheat closed 1/4 cent a bushel lower to 3-3/4 up with July up 1/2 at $3.22. September was unchanged at $3.29-1/2.

NYMEX gasoline futures, catching onto bullishness sweeping through spot gasoline markets Friday, settled higher and dragged a sleepy crude market along for part of the ride, traders said. The gasoline move that brought August futures to a settlement 0.66 cent higher at 59.26 cents a gallon, was tangled in a web of intrigue that involved an independent Gulf Coast trading house, a Wall Street giant and other traders. But crude trade was dampened by the waiting surrounding the restart of limited Iraqi oil sales, with traders eager to here about a key meeting on Sunday in Baghdad that should signal how quickly those sales
might resume. August crude settled 11 cents higher at $19.33 a barrel after a session of traders sitting on the fence.
